subject: Reserved Commit economics & capacity lexicon — follow-up and redlines
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@lumenixhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@lumenixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying Reserved Commit math and SLA credit ladder

Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is working through the RFP and there are a few open items we need clarified before we can move to legal. Attached is the relevant section from our RFP. Main asks: 1) how Redwood defines a single "Capacity Unit" (we need this to map to our internal forecasting), 2) how reserved commit discounts are applied over the billing period (amortized vs upfront), and 3) the exact SLA/service-credit ladder (we need p50/p95 latency targets called out).

From our side: we prefer a 12-month amortization rather than a single upfront prepay for budgeting reasons. We also need a transparent mapping from committed GPU-hours to expected throughput for our typical inference mix (chat + less-than-2k tokens generation). Can you send a short economics example showing committed units, discount rate, and amortized monthly charge?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Samantha
Director, Procurement
Lumenix Health
Attachment: RFP_Lumenix_Q2_2027.pdf (PDF, 118 KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@lumenixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying Reserved Commit math and SLA credit ladder

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear list. TL;DR: 
- Capacity Unit = 1 reserved vGPU-hour (see definition below).
- Discounts can be amortized monthly or taken as prepaid credit; we’ll show both examples.
- SLA: we publish latency SLOs per route and a credit ladder; can provide p50/p95 buckets and an explicit remedy ladder you can attach to SOW.

I attached our current "Capacity Definition" PDF; Dev will send a price sheet with amortization math and suggested tiers. Marissa (legal) will follow up on the contract language you referenced.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Wed 4/14 to walk the amortization table and agree on the wording for Capacity Unit and the service credit ladder. Does 10:00am PT work?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Dedicated
Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity-definition-v1.pdf (PDF, 42 KB)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: draft pricing tiers & amortization examples for Lumenix

Team —

Putting here what I plan to present on Wed: concise pricing mechanics so we don't improvise on the call. Numbers are illustrative (we'll finalize after legal redlines):

- Unit definition: 1 Capacity Unit (CU) = 1 reserved vGPU-hour on our Dedicated pool (NVIDIA L40s equivalent). CU can be pooled and shared across model endpoints; billing accrues per CU consumed.

- Discount tiers (applied to list monthly rate, then amortized):
  * 6-month commit: 10%
  * 12-month commit: 18%
  * 24-month commit: 25%

- Amortization example (12-month, 10k CUs):
  * List monthly (no discount): $0.50 per CU-hour -> $5,000/month
  * 18% discount amortized -> $4,100/month effective
  * If prepaid, customer gets the same net discount applied at invoice time, but cashflow differs.

- Throughput guidance: for typical chat mix (avg 600 tokens/session, P50 gen latency target 120ms per token), 1k CUs sustained supports approx 80 QPS of lightweight chat; we'll provide a tailored throughput map once we see their request distribution.

Attachments: proposed-pricing-sheet.xlsx (Excel). I'll bring the sheet to the call and walk a couple of allocation scenarios.

—Dev
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@lumenixhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@lumenixhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying Reserved Commit math and SLA credit ladder

Kimberly/Dev —

Thanks for the quick materials and scheduling the call. Two items we need clarified before legal is comfortable:

1) SLA credits: our counsel wants p50/p95 latency bands expressed as explicit thresholds in the contract and a clear credit percentage per breach tier (we usually see a 5/10/20% ladder for increasing severity).

2) Capacity Unit footnote: we need to capture the exact baseline image/config that defines a "vGPU-hour" (GPU type, memory, burst behavior) — otherwise our ops team cannot map to cloud runbook estimates.

If you can provide a short paragraph that can be pasted into the SOW that defines CU in terms we can operationalize, that'll speed things up.

Also, on amortization: prefer monthly amortization (our CFO). If you can provide monthly amortized invoice examples (prepaid vs monthly charge), it helps the finance team sign off.

Samantha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lumenix — proposed contract language (redlines)

Folks —

I reviewed the excerpt of the Master Services Agreement Lumenix shared and drafted redlines. Key points I edited:
- Suggest replacing the broad term "Capacity Unit" with a defined paragraph: 
  "Capacity Unit (CU): one (1) reserved vGPU-hour, measured on an hourly basis, on a single physical GPU or partitioned vGPU instance equivalent to NVIDIA L40-class performance, with 24 GiB of available GPU memory for model inference. CU consumption is measured at the aggregate account level; unused CUs do not roll forward unless explicitly stated in the SOW."

- Tightened SLA remedy ladder to explicit percentages tied to availability windows and latency bands (p50/p95). Proposed remedies are credits applied as a percentage of the monthly fee for the affected route.

- Added a carve-out for model-induced latency spikes: credits will not apply when increased latency is attributable to customer models or prompt patterns, agreed in writing via tracing traces.

I attached the redline doc; please review and confirm if we are ok to send this to Lumenix as our response. If yes, I'll incorporate their suggested edits and track changes.

Attachment: redlines_Lumenix_dedicated.docx (DOCX, 28 KB)

—Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@lumenixhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved Commit economics & capacity lexicon — follow-up and redlines

Samantha —

Appreciate the questions. Attached is an updated "Capacity Definition" PDF that reflects Marissa's suggested paragraph; we also exported two amortization examples (prepaid vs monthly) from Dev's sheet and included a throughput mapping for a 12-month, 10k CU commit. Summary below:

- CU definition: we accept Marissa's language with one tweak clarifying "partitioned vGPU instance" applies only when explicitly referenced in SOW.
- SLA ladder: we will publish route-level p50/p95 targets in the SOW; proposed remedy ladder: 5%/10%/20% of affected route monthly spend for increasing severity.
- Pricing: offer stands for 12-month commit at 18% discount amortized monthly; if Lumenix prepays, we'll apply same 18% as an upfront credit.

Next steps: if acceptable, Marissa will send the redlines to you as a tracked-change Word doc and I'll push an updated SOW and DocuSign envelope. Linking HubSpot deal here for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/2345234/record/LUM-2027-001

Attachments: capacity-definition-v2.pdf, proposed-pricing-sheet.xlsx

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@lumenixhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@lumenixhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved Commit economics & capacity lexicon — follow-up and redlines

Kimberly/Team —

Thanks — Lumenix is prepared to move forward on a conditional basis. We agree to a 12-month reserved commit at the 18% amortized discount, with the revised CU language and the SLA ladder you proposed. Two small asks before signature: 

1) carve out explicit wording to ensure credits are not automatically triggered for customer-caused model issues; we appreciate Marissa's clause and ask for one sentence clarifying the process for attribution (traces + 72-hour investigation window).
2) add a termination-for-convenience notice window to the SOW (60 days) with a pro-rata reconciliation clause for unused amortized CUs.

If you can incorporate those two items in the SOW, we'll be ready to sign and route DocuSign to our procurement team. Please send the updated SOW and DocuSign link when ready.

Samantha Lee
Director, Procurement
Lumenix Health
